verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe the Sai API, which lets developers send plain-language tasks from their own code or coding agents. It is offered as a REST API, a Python SDK and an MCP server, with concrete documented endpoints such as GET /v1/agents/events, POST /v1/agents/approve and GET /v1/agents/machines. A probe found llms.txt but no published OpenAPI/Swagger spec at the standard paths; that is a documentation-depth gap, not a contradiction. Missing for 10: a machine-readable OpenAPI spec, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the API in use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Developers can drive Sai from their own code or coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) with the Sai API: send a task in plain language, and Sai completes it on a cloud Windows computer.
gives developers, their code and their coding agents the same autonomous computer through a REST API, a Python SDK and an MCP server.
`GET /v1/agents/events` streams progress; `POST /v1/agents/approve` answers an approval request; `GET /v1/agents/machines` lists your computers.
